newsitem.title: USA: Trump terminates talks on Colony investment.
newsitem.headline: Trump terminates talks on Colony investment.

text.p: Trump Hotels & Casino Resources Inc said Thursday it has terminated negotiations regarding the proposed investment by a Colony Capital Inc subsidiary in Trump's Castle Associates, the owner of Trump's Castle Casino Resort in Atlantic City, N.J.
It said it intends to complete its "retheming" of Trump's Castle to Trump Marina by July and is reevaluating plans to construct a new hotel tower at the property.
Trump Hotels also disclosed that palintiffs in a pending lawsuit relating to Trump Hotels' purchase of Trump's Castle in 1996 have amended the complaint.
The amended complaint now includes claims against Colony for "aiding and abetting" certain violations alleged in the lawsuit and seeks to stop the Colony transaction, Trump Hotels said.
A Trump Hotels spokesman was not immediately available to explain reasons for the termination of the negotiations.
A source familiar with the negotiations said, however, that Trump Hotels may have decided on the termination to avoid spending big fees that could develop in continuing litigation.
In January, Trump Hotels said it signed a letter of intent to form a partnership with Colony, which would invest $125 million to fund the expansion and retheming of Trump's Castle.

The Los Angeles-based Colony would make its investment by buying a 51 percent stake in Trump's Castle while Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Holdings LP would retain a 49 percent stake while continuing to manage the property.
